newsitem.title: UK: Save Children Fund denies Somalia kidnapping.
newsitem.headline: Save Children Fund denies Somalia kidnapping.

text.p: The British-based Save the Children Fund charity on Saturday denied a report that one of its aid workers had been kidnapped in Somalia.
"The report is innacurate. No one has been kidnapped. All our staff are safe and well and we know where they are," spokeswoman Jenny Meadows told Reuters.
Meadows said there had been a "minor bureaucratic misunderstanding" on Friday night involving staff in a camp near the border with Ethiopia. "It is inaccurate to call it a kidnap", she said.
Meadows said the Save the Children Fund in London was checking with local field workers to establish what had happened and hoped to get a fuller picture later on Saturday.

Somali businessmen had earlier told Reuters in Mogadishu that an unnamed British woman working with the charity was taken away in the border town of Feerfeer by unidentified gunmen on Friday night. Three of her Somali colleagues were also taken.
But aid agency sources in the Kenyan capital Nairobi played down the incident, saying talks were being held with a local militia group "to sort out a few misunderstandings."
